newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump, up seven days in a row.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump, up seven days in a row.

text.p: Slovenian shares added on another 1.98 percent on Wednesday to take their winning streak to seven days in a row.
Traders said they expect the rally to continue on the back of renewed optimism and the return of foreign investors.

"Foreign investors have been lured to the market by the new listing of shares of newly privatised companies. This has brought fresh capital and with it a lot of optimism. That could continue to push prices up until the end of October," one said.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 20.92 points to 1,078.35.
* 11 shares rose and seven fell, while six were untraded.
* Turnover fell to 371.9 million tolars from 635.9 million.
* Lek's A issue was the most actively traded, falling 1.47 percent to 18,882 tolars on volume of 10,429 shares for total turnover of 196.9 million tolars.
* Financial consultancy Dadas was the biggest gainer, surging 39.68 percent to 28,201 tolars on volume of 915 shares for total turnover of 25.8 million tolars.
Brokers said Dadas' steep rise was in reaction to its low share price, which is currently 88.4 percent cheaper than at the end of March.
* Bank UBK was the leading decliner, falling 3.08 percent to 7,803 tolars on volume of 65 shares for total turnover of 507,000 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
